dandiset.yaml.name: Cholinergic interneuron control of intrastriatal GABAergic circuits targeting spiny projection neurons is disrupted in Parkinson’s disease models
dandiset.yaml.description: Whole-cell voltage clamp recordings examining cholinergic interneuron (ChI) synaptic transmission  to striatal spiny projection neurons (SPNs) in mice. This dataset characterizes ChI-evoked  postsynaptic currents (PSCs) in both direct pathway SPNs (dSPNs, expressing Drd1a) and indirect  pathway SPNs (iSPNs, expressing Drd2) in the dorsolateral striatum. Recordings were performed  at P80-90 using optogenetic stimulation of ChIs expressing Chronos. ChI-evoked responses were  characterized in control conditions and with pharmacological blockers (GABAzine to block GABAergic  transmission; Mecamylamine to block nicotinic receptors) to dissect the relative contributions of  cholinergic and GABAergic components. Both dSPNs and iSPNs showed complex PSCs with fast and slow  components, reflecting direct cholinergic input and indirect GABAergic transmission via ChI activation  of GABAergic interneurons. This dataset provides baseline characterization of ChI-SPN synaptic  transmission in the healthy adult striatum.
dandiset.yaml.protocol: Whole-cell voltage clamp recordings from identified dSPNs and iSPNs in acute striatal slices  from adult mice (P80-90). AAV-EF1a-FLEX-Chronos-GFP was injected into the dorsolateral striatum  for optogenetic stimulation of cholinergic interneurons. Recordings were performed in control  conditions and with sequential application of pharmacological blockers: GABAzine (GABA_A receptor  antagonist) to isolate cholinergic components, and Mecamylamine (nicotinic receptor antagonist)  to assess nicotinic contribution. Recordings were filtered at 2 kHz and digitized at 10 kHz using  Clampex 10.7 software.

data_collection.session_description: Whole-cell voltage clamp recording from striatal spiny projection neurons during optogenetic stimulation of cholinergic interneurons
data_collection.experiment_description: Optogenetic activation of cholinergic interneurons during whole-cell voltage clamp recordings  to characterize ChI synaptic transmission to both dSPNs and iSPNs. ChI-evoked PSCs showed  complex kinetics with fast and slow components. The fast component was primarily cholinergic  (blocked by Mecamylamine), while the slow component was largely GABAergic (blocked by GABAzine),  reflecting ChI-mediated activation of GABAergic interneurons. Both dSPNs and iSPNs received  similar patterns of ChI input, suggesting ChIs provide broad modulation of striatal output  pathways in the healthy adult brain.

dandiset.yaml.name: CRISPR-mediated knockdown of GABA-A receptor delta subunit effects on cholinergic synaptic transmission to striatal neurons
dandiset.yaml.description: Whole-cell voltage clamp recordings examining the role of GABA-A receptor delta subunit in  cholinergic interneuron (ChI) synaptic transmission to striatal spiny projection neurons (SPNs).  This dataset uses CRISPR-Cas9 mediated knockdown of the Gabrd gene (encoding the delta subunit)  to investigate delta-containing GABA-A receptors in striatal cholinergic signaling. Recordings  were performed at P80-90 using optogenetic stimulation of ChIs expressing Chronos. Two experimental  groups were compared: CRISPR control (AAV9-Syn-FRed-U6gRGABAd + AAV9-Syn-flex-rc-chronos-td) and  CRISPR delta KD (AAV9-Syn-FRed-U6gRGABAd + AAV9-Syn-saCas-mWPRE-hGHPloyA + AAV9-Syn-flex-rc-chronos-td).  ChI-evoked responses were characterized to determine the contribution of delta-containing GABA-A  receptors to cholinergic transmission in the striatum. This dataset provides insight into the  molecular mechanisms underlying ChI-SPN synaptic communication.
dandiset.yaml.protocol: Whole-cell voltage clamp recordings from SPNs in acute striatal slices from adult mice (P80-90).  Mice received stereotaxic injections of AAV vectors for CRISPR-mediated delta subunit knockdown  and Cre-dependent Chronos expression in cholinergic interneurons. Control group received  AAV9-Syn-FRed-U6gRGABAd + AAV9-Syn-flex-rc-chronos-td. Delta KD group received  AAV9-Syn-FRed-U6gRGABAd + AAV9-Syn-saCas-mWPRE-hGHPloyA + AAV9-Syn-flex-rc-chronos-td.  Recordings were performed 2-3 weeks post-injection for optogenetic stimulation of ChIs.  Recordings were filtered at 2 kHz and digitized at 10 kHz using Clampex 10.7 software.  Holding potential -80 mV.

data_collection.session_description: Whole-cell voltage clamp recording from striatal spiny projection neurons during optogenetic stimulation of cholinergic interneurons with CRISPR delta subunit manipulation
data_collection.experiment_description: Optogenetic activation of cholinergic interneurons during whole-cell voltage clamp recordings  to assess the role of delta-containing GABA-A receptors in ChI synaptic transmission. CRISPR-Cas9  mediated knockdown of Gabrd was used to reduce delta subunit expression. ChI-evoked responses  were compared between control and delta KD conditions to determine the contribution of delta-containing  receptors to ChI-mediated synaptic transmission in striatal circuits.
data_collection.virus: AAV9-Syn-FRed-U6gRGABAd + AAV9-Syn-flex-rc-chronos-td (control); AAV9-Syn-FRed-U6gRGABAd + AAV9-Syn-saCas-mWPRE-hGHPloyA + AAV9-Syn-flex-rc-chronos-td (delta KD)

dandiset.yaml.name: NDNF+ neurogliaform interneuron synaptic transmission to striatal projection neurons
dandiset.yaml.description: Whole-cell voltage clamp recordings examining NDNF+ neurogliaform interneuron synaptic transmission  to striatal spiny projection neurons (SPNs). This dataset characterizes NDNF-evoked GABAergic  postsynaptic currents in both direct pathway SPNs (dSPNs, expressing Drd1a-eGFP) and indirect  pathway SPNs (iSPNs, expressing Drd2-eGFP) in the dorsolateral striatum. Recordings were performed  at P80-90 using optogenetic stimulation of NDNF+ neurogliaform interneurons expressing Chronos.  Both iSPNs and dSPNs were recorded and analyzed together to characterize NDNF-mediated GABAergic  inhibition of striatal output neurons. This dataset provides insight into the role of neurogliaform  interneurons in striatal circuit modulation.
dandiset.yaml.protocol: Whole-cell voltage clamp recordings from identified dSPNs and iSPNs in acute striatal slices  from adult mice (P80-90). NDNF-Flp mice were crossed with either Drd2-eGFP or Drd1a-eGFP lines  for SPN identification. AAV-DIO-flpo-Chronos was injected into the dorsolateral striatum for  optogenetic stimulation of NDNF+ neurogliaform interneurons. Both iSPNs and dSPNs were recorded  and analyzed together. Recordings were filtered at 2 kHz and digitized at 10 kHz using  Clampex 10.7 software.

data_collection.session_description: Whole-cell voltage clamp recording from striatal spiny projection neurons during optogenetic stimulation of NDNF+ neurogliaform interneurons
data_collection.experiment_description: Optogenetic activation of NDNF+ neurogliaform interneurons during voltage clamp recordings to examine synaptic responses in striatal projection neurons

dandiset.yaml.name: Cholinergic interneuron control of intrastriatal GABAergic circuits targeting spiny projection neurons is disrupted in Parkinson’s disease models
dandiset.yaml.description: Whole-cell voltage-clamp recordings from adult ChAT-ChR2-eYFP mice examining optogenetically evoked responses in striatal spiny projection neurons after unilateral 6-OHDA lesion of the substantia nigra pars compacta. ChR2-expressing cholinergic interneurons were stimulated with blue light while SPNs were recorded in acute coronal brain slices.
dandiset.yaml.protocol: Experiments were performed in adult ChAT-ChR2-eYFP mice (Tg(Chat-COP4*H134R/eYFP, Slc18a3)6Gfng/J). Unilateral dopamine lesions were induced by stereotaxic injection of 6-hydroxydopamine hydrobromide (6-OHDA) dissolved at 3.5 mg/mL in 0.1% ascorbic acid. Mice received unilateral injections into the substantia nigra pars compacta (SNc) at AP -2.7 mm, ML +1.35 mm, DV -4.2 mm from bregma using a Nanoject II Auto-Nanoliter Injector, delivering 1.3 uL total volume at 13.8 nL/5 s. The contralateral hemisphere received saline injections and served as control. Mice were anesthetized with ketamine (80 mg/kg) and xylazine (20 mg/kg), then transcardially perfused with ice-cold NMDG-based cutting solution.  Coronal brain sections were cut at 300 um using a VT1200S vibratome, incubated in oxygenated NMDG solution at 35 C for 5 min, and transferred  to oxygenated aCSF at room temperature until recording. During recordings, slices were perfused with oxygenated aCSF at 32-34 C at 2-4 mL/min.  SPNs were visualized with an Olympus BX50-WI microscope using a 40x water-immersion objective and infrared differential interference contrast  optics. Whole-cell voltage-clamp recordings were performed using borosilicate glass electrodes filled with CsCl-based internal solution. Signals were recorded using a MultiClamp 700B amplifier, digitized using an ITC-1600 digitizer, and acquired using Axograph X software. ChR2-expressing CINs were stimulated using 2 ms blue light pulses at 450 nm delivered every 30 s.

data_collection.session_description: Whole-cell voltage-clamp recordings from striatal SPNs during optogenetic stimulation of ChR2-expressing cholinergic interneurons in adult ChAT-ChR2-eYFP mice with unilateral 6-OHDA lesions.
data_collection.experiment_description: ChR2-expressing cholinergic interneurons were activated with 2 ms, 450 nm blue light pulses delivered every 30 s while SPNs were recorded in voltage clamp. The contralateral saline-injected hemisphere served as control for the unilateral 6-OHDA-lesioned hemisphere.

slice_preparation.incubation: oxygenated NMDG solution at 35 C for 5 min
slice_preparation.holding_solution: oxygenated artificial cerebrospinal fluid at room temperature

acquisition_notes: Axograph data were sampled at 20 kHz.
MATLAB data was acquired using CED Signal and sampled at 25 kHz.
Axograph data used an ITC-1600 digitizer, MultiClamp 700B amplifier, and Axograph acquisition software.
MATLAB files used a CED micro1401kii board, MultiClamp 700B amplifier, and Signal (CED) acquisition software.
No drugs were in the solution.
All stimulations were performed at 1000 ms in the checked samples.
Holding potential was -70 mV with CsCl internal solution.

dandiset.yaml.name: Prodromal Parkinsonian state enhances cholinergic interneuron-evoked acetylcholine release in dorsolateral striatum
dandiset.yaml.description: Two-photon imaging experiments examining cholinergic interneuron (ChI)-evoked acetylcholine (ACh) release dynamics in the dorsolateral striatum (DLS) of prodromal MCI-Park mice and littermate  controls. Acetylcholine signaling was monitored using the genetically encoded fluorescent sensor GRABACh3.0 expressed in the DLS. Acute striatal slices were electrically stimulated and ACh transients measured using two-photon laser scanning microscopy (2PLSM). In both control and prodromal MCI-Park mice, evoked fluorescence responses rose rapidly and decayed back to baseline within seconds. However, the amplitude of evoked ACh transients was significantly larger in prodromal MCI-Park mice, suggesting that cholinergic signaling in the prodromal striatum is disinhibited prior to the development of overt parkinsonian network pathology. These findings support the hypothesis that loss of dopaminergic signaling alone is sufficient to enhance ChI-evoked ACh release through reduced inhibitory signaling mediated by presynaptic dopamine D2 receptors
dandiset.yaml.protocol: Acetylcholine dynamics were evaluated using the genetically encoded fluorescent ACh sensor GRABACh3.0 expressed in the dorsolateral striatum. An AAV carrying the GRABACh3.0 expression construct was stereotaxically injected into the DLS of P25 MCI-Park mice and littermate controls. Two weeks later at P40, acute coronal brain slices containing striatal GRABACh3.0 expression were prepared and transferred to a submerged recording chamber continuously superfused with oxygenated ACSF maintained at room temperature. Two-photon imaging was performed using a Chameleon Ultra II two-photon laser tuned to 920 nm coupled to an Ultima In Vitro Multiphoton Microscope system equipped with a 60x/1.0 NA water-immersion objective and GaAsP photomultiplier detector. Fluorescence emission was collected in the 490–560 nm range. Time-series images were acquired at 21.26 frames per second using Galvo spiral scanning mode with a pixel resolution of 0.388 μm × 0.388 μm and 4-μs dwell time per pixel. After a 5-second baseline acquisition period, acetylcholine release was evoked using a concentric bipolar stimulation electrode positioned approximately 150 μm dorsal to the imaging field. Electrical stimulation consisted of a single 1 ms pulse at 0.3 mA. Imaging continued for at least 5 seconds following stimulation. Three stimulation trials were recorded for each region of interest and averaged. Fluorescence intensity values were background-subtracted and normalized to baseline fluorescence using ΔF/F₀.

data_collection.session_description: Two-photon imaging of electrically evoked acetylcholine release in dorsolateral striatum of prodromal MCI-Park mice and littermate controls using the GRABACh3.0 sensor.
data_collection.experiment_description: GRABACh3.0 fluorescence responses were used to quantify evoked acetylcholine release in the dorsolateral striatum. Electrical stimulation evoked rapid fluorescence transients in both control and MCI-Park mice; however, the amplitude of the ACh transient was significantly increased in prodromal MCI-Park mice, indicating enhanced cholinergic signaling associated with loss of dopaminergic inhibition.

dandiset.yaml.name: Cholinergic interneuron control of intrastriatal GABAergic circuits targeting spiny projection neurons is disrupted in Parkinson’s disease models
dandiset.yaml.description: Whole-cell voltage clamp recordings examining cholinergic interneuron (ChI) to spiny projection  neuron (SPN) coupling in prodromal MCI-Park Parkinson's disease model mice. This dataset compares  ChI-evoked postsynaptic currents (PSCs) in SPNs between age-matched control mice (DAT-Cre X ChAT-Flp)  and MCI-Park mice (DAT-Cre X Ndufs2-fl/fl X ChAT-Flp) with ChI-selective ablation of mitochondrial  complex I via Ndufs2 knockout. Recordings were performed at P39-40, two weeks after AAV injection at P25.  At this prodromal stage, MCI-Park mice show virtually absent tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) expression and  dramatically reduced evoked dopamine release, yet exhibit no motor deficits. ChI-evoked PSCs are  significantly smaller in prodromal MCI-Park SPNs compared to controls, despite unchanged PSC kinetics.  This suggests weakened ChI-SPN coupling may be an early pathological feature in Parkinson's disease  progression, occurring before motor symptoms manifest.
dandiset.yaml.protocol: Whole-cell voltage clamp recordings from SPNs in acute striatal slices from control and  prodromal MCI-Park mice. AAV-Flp-dependent Chronos (AAV-fDIO-Chronos) injected at P25 for  optogenetic stimulation of cholinergic interneurons. In MCI-Park mice, additional AAV-Flp-dependent  Cre recombinase (AAV-fDIO-Cre) was injected to ablate Ndufs2 in ChIs. Recordings performed at  P39-40 in control conditions and with pharmacological blockers (AP5+NBQX+CGP55845A to isolate  cholinergic responses; GABAzine to assess GABAergic components).

data_collection.session_description: Whole-cell voltage clamp recording from striatal spiny projection neurons during optogenetic stimulation of cholinergic interneurons in prodromal MCI-Park model
data_collection.experiment_description: Optogenetic activation of cholinergic interneurons in MCI-Park model mice during whole-cell  voltage clamp recordings to examine ChI-SPN coupling and synaptic responses in prodromal  parkinsonian state. The working hypothesis was that ChI coupling to tyrosine hydroxylase  positive (TH+) and neurogliaform interneurons (NGFIs) would be strengthened in prodromal  MCI-Park mice, leading to enhanced GABAergic responses in SPNs. Unexpectedly, ChI-evoked  PSCs in SPNs from prodromal MCI-Park mice were significantly smaller than controls (both  peak and total charge transfer), although PSC kinetics remained unaltered. This indicates  that reduced ChI-SPN coupling is an early feature of parkinsonian pathology, occurring  before motor symptom onset.
data_collection.virus: AAV-Flp-dependent Chronos (AAV-fDIO-Chronos); AAV-Flp-dependent Cre (AAV-fDIO-Cre) for MCI-Park mice

dandiset.yaml.name: Cholinergic interneuron synaptic transmission to striatal projection neurons in 6-OHDA Parkinson model
dandiset.yaml.description: Whole-cell voltage clamp recordings examining cholinergic interneuron (ChI) synaptic transmission  to direct and indirect pathway striatal spiny projection neurons (SPNs) in 6-OHDA lesioned mice.  This dataset compares ChI-evoked postsynaptic currents (PSCs) in both dSPNs (expressing Drd1a-tdTomato)  and iSPNs (expressing Drd2-eGFP) between healthy control mice and mice with unilateral 6-OHDA  lesions of the medial forebrain bundle (MFB). Recordings were performed 4 weeks post-lesion at P80-90  using optogenetic stimulation of ChIs expressing Chronos. ChI-evoked responses were characterized  in control conditions and with pharmacological blockers (AP5+NBQX+CGP55845A to isolate cholinergic  components; GABAzine to assess GABAergic contributions; Mecamylamine to block nicotinic receptors;  Carbenoxolone to block gap junctions). This dataset examines how severe dopamine depletion affects  ChI-SPN synaptic transmission in both direct and indirect pathway neurons.
dandiset.yaml.protocol: Whole-cell voltage clamp recordings from identified dSPNs and iSPNs in acute striatal slices  from control and 6-OHDA lesioned mice (P80-90). AAV-EF1a-FLEX-Chronos-GFP was injected into  the dorsolateral striatum for optogenetic stimulation of cholinergic interneurons. Lesioned  mice received unilateral 6-OHDA injection into the medial forebrain bundle (MFB) to ablate  dopaminergic neurons. Recordings were performed 4 weeks post-lesion in control conditions  and with sequential application of pharmacological blockers: AP5+NBQX+CGP55845A (glutamate  and GABA-B receptor antagonists) to isolate cholinergic components, GABAzine (GABA-A receptor  antagonist), Mecamylamine (nicotinic receptor antagonist), and Carbenoxolone (gap junction  blocker). Recordings were filtered at 2 kHz and digitized at 10 kHz using Clampex 10.7 software.

data_collection.session_description: Whole-cell voltage clamp recording from striatal spiny projection neurons during optogenetic stimulation of cholinergic interneurons in 6-OHDA lesioned mice
data_collection.experiment_description: Optogenetic activation of cholinergic interneurons during whole-cell voltage clamp recordings  to examine how severe dopamine depletion affects ChI synaptic transmission to both dSPNs and  iSPNs. The 6-OHDA lesion model provides a severe, acute dopamine depletion paradigm to assess  ChI-SPN coupling in late-stage parkinsonism. ChI-evoked PSCs were characterized across both  SPN subtypes in control and lesioned conditions to determine pathway-specific changes in  cholinergic transmission following dopamine loss.

dandiset.yaml.name: Cholinergic interneuron control of intrastriatal GABAergic circuits targeting spiny projection neurons is disrupted in Parkinson’s disease models
dandiset.yaml.description: Whole-cell voltage clamp recordings examining NPY+ interneuron GABAergic transmission  to direct and indirect pathway striatal spiny projection neurons (SPNs) in 6-OHDA lesioned mice.  NPY+ interneurons include both TH-expressing low-threshold spiking interneurons (TH-LTS) and  neurogliaform interneurons (NGFs). This dataset compares NPY+-evoked postsynaptic currents (PSCs)  in both dSPNs (expressing Drd1a-tdTomato) and iSPNs (expressing Drd2-eGFP) between healthy control  mice and mice with unilateral 6-OHDA lesions of the medial forebrain bundle (MFB). AAV-DIO-Chronos  was injected into the dorsolateral striatum on the same day as 6-OHDA lesioning. Recordings were  performed 4 weeks post-lesion at P80-90 using optogenetic stimulation of NPY+ interneurons.  NPY+-evoked responses were characterized in control conditions and with pharmacological blockers  (AP5+NBQX+CGP55845A to isolate GABAergic components; GABAzine to confirm GABA-A receptor mediation;  Sulpiride to assess D2 receptor modulation). This dataset examines how severe dopamine depletion  affects NPY+ interneuron to SPN GABAergic transmission in both direct and indirect pathway neurons.
dandiset.yaml.protocol: Whole-cell voltage clamp recordings from identified dSPNs and iSPNs in acute striatal slices  from control and 6-OHDA lesioned mice (P80-90). NPY-Cre mice were crossed with either Drd1a-tdTomato  or Drd2-eGFP transgenic lines for SPN identification. AAV-Cre-dependent Chronos (AAV-DIO-Chronos)  was injected into the dorsolateral striatum for optogenetic stimulation of NPY+ interneurons,  which include both TH-expressing low-threshold spiking interneurons (TH-LTS) and neurogliaform  interneurons (NGFs). For lesioned mice, unilateral 6-OHDA was injected into the medial forebrain  bundle (MFB) on the same day as AAV injection to ablate dopaminergic neurons. Recordings were  performed 4 weeks post-lesion in control conditions and with pharmacological blockers:  AP5+NBQX+CGP55845A (glutamate and GABA-B receptor antagonists) to isolate GABAergic components,  GABAzine (GABA-A receptor antagonist) to confirm GABA-A mediation, and Sulpiride (D2 receptor  antagonist) to assess dopaminergic modulation. Recordings were filtered at 2 kHz and digitized  at 10 kHz using Clampex 10.7 software.

data_collection.session_description: Whole-cell voltage clamp recording from striatal spiny projection neurons during optogenetic stimulation of NPY+ interneurons in control and 6-OHDA lesioned mice
data_collection.experiment_description: Optogenetic activation of NPY+ interneurons (TH-LTS and NGFs) during whole-cell voltage clamp  recordings to examine how severe dopamine depletion affects GABAergic interneuron transmission  to both dSPNs and iSPNs. The 6-OHDA lesion model provides a severe, acute dopamine depletion  paradigm to assess NPY+ interneuron to SPN coupling in late-stage parkinsonism. NPY+-evoked  IPSCs were characterized across both SPN subtypes in control and lesioned conditions to  determine pathway-specific changes in GABAergic transmission following dopamine loss.

dandiset.yaml.name: Cholinergic interneuron control of intrastriatal GABAergic circuits targeting spiny projection neurons is disrupted in Parkinson’s disease models
dandiset.yaml.description: Whole-cell voltage clamp recordings examining functional connectivity from striatal cholinergic interneurons (ChIs) to NDNF+ neurogliaform interneurons (NGFs) in the dorsolateral striatum of control and 6-OHDA lesioned mice. NDNF+ NGFs were identified using Flp-dependent mCherry expression in ChAT-Cre x NDNF-Flp mice. Cholinergic interneurons were optogenetically stimulated following injection of AAV-Cre-dependent Chronos, while NDNF+ NGFs were labeled with AAV-Flp-dependent mCherry. Recordings were performed 4 weeks after viral injection in control mice or 4 weeks post-lesion in mice with unilateral 6-OHDA lesions of the medial forebrain bundle (MFB). This dataset examines how severe dopamine depletion alters ChI-to-NGF functional connectivity in the striatum.
dandiset.yaml.protocol: Whole-cell voltage clamp recordings were obtained from NDNF+ neurogliaform interneurons in acute striatal slices from ChAT-Cre x NDNF-Flp mice. NDNF-expressing NGFs were visually identified by Flp-dependent mCherry expression following stereotaxic injection of AAV-Flp-dependent mCherry into the dorsolateral striatum. Cholinergic interneurons were optogenetically stimulated using AAV-Cre-dependent Chronos injected into the same region. In 6-OHDA lesioned mice, unilateral 6-OHDA was injected into the medial forebrain bundle (MFB) to lesion dopaminergic neurons. Recordings were performed 4 weeks after injection or lesion. Signals were filtered at 2 kHz and digitized at 10 kHz using Clampex 10.7 software with an Axon Multiclamp 700B patch clamp amplifier.

data_collection.session_description: Whole-cell voltage clamp recording from NDNF+ neurogliaform interneurons during optogenetic stimulation of cholinergic interneurons in control and 6-OHDA lesioned mice
data_collection.experiment_description: Optogenetic activation of cholinergic interneurons during whole-cell voltage clamp recordings from NDNF+ neurogliaform interneurons to examine ChI-NGF functional connectivity in the dorsolateral striatum under control conditions and after severe dopamine depletion induced by unilateral 6-OHDA lesion.

dandiset.yaml.name: Cholinergic interneuron control of intrastriatal GABAergic circuits targeting spiny projection neurons is disrupted in Parkinson’s disease models
dandiset.yaml.description: Multiplex fluorescent RNAscope dataset examining Chrnb2 transcript expression in dorsal striatal interneurons from control and unilateral 6-OHDA lesioned mice. Tissue was collected four weeks after lesioning and labeled with probes targeting CHRNB2, TH, and NDNF to identify TH-expressing interneurons and NDNF-expressing neurogliaform interneurons. Sections were imaged with confocal microscopy, and Chrnb2-positive puncta were quantified within manually defined cellular ROIs. The dataset compares Chrnb2 signal per cell between control and lesioned sides of the striatum to test whether dopamine depletion alters nicotinic receptor beta2 subunit expression in these interneuron populations.
dandiset.yaml.protocol: ChAT-Cre mice were sacrificed four weeks after unilateral 6-OHDA lesioning.  Brain tissue was rapidly collected, embedded in OCT, flash frozen, and sectioned coronally at 12 um.  RNAscope multiplex fluorescent in situ hybridization was performed on fresh frozen sections using the  RNAscope Multiplex Fluorescent Detection Kit v2 with probes against CHRNB2, NDNF, and TH.  Slides were mounted with DAPI-containing antifade medium and imaged on an Olympus FluoView FV10i confocal microscope.  TH-positive and NDNF-positive interneurons in dorsal striatum were identified from their respective fluorescence  channels and manually outlined as cellular ROIs by the experimenter. Chrnb2-positive puncta were counted manually within each  ROI and recorded as replicate-level counts for each cell/ROI. Each count was linked to the corresponding imaging field,  hemisphere, condition, cell type, and session. The unlesioned hemisphere was labeled Intact and the 6-OHDA-lesioned  hemisphere was labeled Lesioned.
